newsitem.title: JAPAN: Decision seen soon on U.S. envoy to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Decision seen soon on U.S. envoy to Japan.

text.p: The United States is likely to make a decision soon on its next ambassador to Japan, former U.S. trade representative William Brock said on Tuesday.

"My expectation is that you will see some very quick action regarding Japan. I can't tell you who or when, but I think you know who and I think it will be soon," Brock told a news conference by the U.S.-Japan 21st Century Committee, a group of opinion leaders from the two nations which held a meeting in Japan from May 24 to 26. Media reports said in April that former U.S. House Speaker Tom Foley was likely to be appointed to replace Walter Mondale, who resigned as envoy in December.
Foley had been scheduled to attend the two-day forum in Japan but did not do so, Brock said.
"I have a very clear understanding of why Mr Foley is not here, but I'm not at liberty to talk about it," he said.

Brock said the U.S. appointment process had been "waxing exceedingly slow in a number of areas" partly because of competing pressures on the administration, including a discussion over on a balanced budget agreement.

The U.S. Senate on Friday approved a five-year plan to balance the federal budget and cut taxes. The House passed its version last Wednesday and now differences between the two versions must be worked out.
